name: LinkButton
usage: Edit, archive and remove in table rows; clickable names in lists; "View" and "Pin" on cards

props.name: tone
props.description:
Tone: `accent` (default); `danger` for destructive inline actions such as removing an item or revoking
access.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon before the text: a name, or an icon component such as Lucide's `Plus`.

props.name: disabledReason
props.description:
Disabled reason: an explanation shown on hover or keyboard focus while `disabled` (as on Button). With a
reason, the button can still be focused with `Tab` (`aria-disabled`), screen readers read the reason through
`aria-describedby`, and clicks and `Enter` have no effect.

types.name: IconName
types.summary:
Name of a registered icon. Only the icons listed here can be used; they are Lucide icons under shorter names
(`trash` is Lucide's `Trash2`, `more` is `Ellipsis`). All names at runtime: `iconNames`. Props that take an
icon also accept an icon component instead of a name (see IconComponent).

types.name: IconComponent
types.summary:
An icon component, such as Lucide's `Plus` (`import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'`), accepted wherever an icon name
is: `<Button icon={Plus}>`, `<Icon icon={Plus} />`, menu items and so on. Names (`icon="plus"`) are convenient
and work in data such as menu configurations, but cover only the registered icons (`iconNames`); a component can
be any Lucide icon, or an SVG of your own. Both are drawn with the same size, stroke width and `tone`.

types.name: IconComponentProps
types.summary:
Props that Icon passes to an icon component. Lucide icons (`import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'`) accept them; a
component of another icon set, or an SVG of your own, works too if it accepts them, or passes them on to its
`<svg>`.

fields.name: strokeWidth
fields.description:
Stroke width in the units of a 24 × 24 view box, already scaled for `size`: the line is 1.75 px wide on screen
by default, whatever the size.

fields.name: color
fields.description:
Stroke color: `currentColor` (the text color) or a semantic color variable, such as
`var(--vl-color-danger)`.

fields.name: aria-hidden
fields.description: `true` for a decorative icon (hidden from screen readers).

fields.name: aria-label
fields.description: Accessible name of a meaningful icon.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description:
Accent-colored text without background or underline; the font size follows its context. Use it for edit and
archive actions in table rows and for "View" on cards.

examples.name: InlineName
examples.title: Clickable name
examples.description:
A name in a list that opens its details: it does not stand out awkwardly in running text, and its click area
extends 4 px beyond the text on each side.

examples.name: Danger
examples.title: Destructive actions
examples.description:
Use `tone="danger"` for destructive actions in a row, such as removing or revoking access; irreversible actions
still need a confirmation (Popconfirm or useConfirmDanger).

examples.name: Disabled
examples.title: Disabled and disabled reason
examples.description:
When a button is disabled because of permissions or unmet conditions, explain why with `disabledReason`: it
appears on hover or keyboard focus, and screen readers read it too.
